section_1.title: The Problem: Context and Ambiguity
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge of understanding language where words change meaning based on surrounding context. Define 'Self-Attention' as the model's ability to 'weigh' the importance of every other word in a sentence relative to the current word.
section_1.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' visual highlights connect 'it' to 'animal' via a glowing path, while in '...because it was too wide,' the path connects to 'street'.

section_2.title: The Mechanics: Query, Key, and Value (Q, K, V)
section_2.content: Introduce the Q, K, V vectors as a Retrieval System. Prerequisite: Basic dot product intuition. Explain that a Query (what I'm looking for) matches against a Key (what is available) to create an Attention Score (relevance), which scales the Value (the information content).
section_2.example: Imagine a library: Your 'Query' is the search term, the 'Keys' are the book titles on the shelf, and the 'Values' are the actual content inside the books you decide to read.

section_3.title: Visualizing the Calculation: Scaled Dot-Product
section_3.content: Describe the mathematical pipeline: (Q × Kᵀ) → Divide by root-d_k → Softmax → Multiply by V. Emphasize that 'Softmax' forces the weights to sum to 1, creating a probability distribution over the words.
section_3.example: An animation showing a heat map: As the model processes 'Bank', the word 'River' lights up bright red (high weight), while 'Finance' remains dim (low weight) based on the surrounding context.

section_4.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture
section_4.content: Explain that one attention pass isn't enough. Multi-head attention allows the model to attend to different types of information simultaneously (e.g., one head focuses on grammar, another on semantic relationships, a third on sentiment).
section_4.example: Three detectives looking at a crime scene: One looks for physical clues (syntax), one looks for emotional motives (sentiment), and one looks for timelines (chronology). Their reports are combined for a total understanding.

section_5.title: Application and Conclusion
section_5.content: Summarize how this mechanism enables LLMs to process long-range dependencies efficiently, moving beyond sequential processing to parallelized global context awareness.
section_5.example: A visual comparison: A sequential reader (RNN) reads word-by-word like a person walking through a maze; a Transformer (Attention) views the whole maze from a drone, seeing all paths simultaneously.
